skill.name: copywriting
skill.description: Helps write, rewrite, and improve persuasive website copy for homepages, landing pages, pricing pages, feature pages, product pages, and about pages.
skill.summary: Write clearer, more persuasive website copy with structured page sections, stronger CTAs, and audience-focused messaging.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

security_audit.summary: All nine static findings were reviewed against the cited source lines and appear to be false positives. The flagged content is markdown guidance, copywriting examples, or inline file names, with no executable command, network access, prompt injection, or data exfiltration intent found.

static_findings.snippet: > Stop chasing invoices. Start getting paid on time.
**Note:** Avoid "In conclusion" at the start of a paragraph. It's overused and signals AI writing.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line is an example headline about invoices in a copywriting framework. It does not request system inspection, command execution, or access to local data.
The line introduces weak testimonial examples to avoid. It is marketing guidance and contains no reconnaissance behavior or instruction to inspect the system.
The cited lines describe using numbered steps in a How It Works section. They do not mention networks, hosts, requests, ports, or collection of external information.
The line is a table of contents entry for phrases that sound like AI writing. It is editorial guidance, not an instruction to inspect or alter system state.
The line warns against an overused transition phrase in prose. It contains no system-level instruction, file access, or reconnaissance intent.
The heading introduces a list of overused writing transitions. It is content-style guidance and does not attempt system reconnaissance.
The backticks are markdown inline code around local context filenames. The instruction is to read an existing context file, not to run shell commands or evaluate Ruby backticks.
The line lists vague marketing words to avoid. It is writing-style guidance and has no system reconnaissance or operational behavior.
The cited heading and examples compare vague versus specific copy. They do not request network probing, external requests, or data collection.

content.value_statement: Website pages often sound vague, inconsistent, or hard to act on. This skill helps write structured, persuasive page copy with clear headlines, CTAs, and section flow.
actual_capabilities: Drafts homepage, landing page, pricing page, feature page, product page, and about page copy.
Creates headlines, subheadlines, CTAs, section headers, body copy, and SEO meta content.
Uses page structure guidance for hero sections, social proof, benefits, objections, and final CTAs.
Provides 2-3 alternative headline or CTA options with rationale.
Applies copywriting principles like clarity, specificity, customer language, and benefits over features.
limitations: Does not perform market research unless the user provides source material or customer context.
Does not verify legal, medical, financial, or compliance claims.
Does not replace dedicated email, popup, offer, or copy-editing skills for those tasks.
Needs product details, audience, proof points, and desired action for stronger output.

use_cases.title: Launch a Landing Page
use_cases.description: Draft a focused page with a clear hero, benefit sections, proof, objections, and final CTA.

use_cases.title: Improve Product Pages
use_cases.description: Turn feature descriptions into benefit-led page sections that explain outcomes and reduce confusion.

use_cases.title: Refresh Pricing Copy
use_cases.description: Clarify plan selection, address purchase anxiety, and make the recommended action easier to understand.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Landing Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new page draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write landing page copy for [product]. The audience is [audience]. The primary action is [CTA]. Include a headline, subheadline, three benefit sections, proof, and final CTA.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite Weak Homepage Copy
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for improving existing copy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this homepage copy to be clearer and more specific. Keep the same offer and audience. Improve the headline, subheadline, CTAs, and section flow. Explain the key changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Pricing Page Messaging
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for conversion-focused pricing pages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create pricing page copy for [product]. Help visitors choose between [plans]. Address likely objections, explain the recommended plan, and write CTAs for each plan.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Page Copy System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt using audience, proof, objections, and tone.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this product context, create a complete page copy system. Include positioning, page structure, section-by-section copy, headline alternatives, CTA alternatives, SEO title, meta description, and rationale for major choices.

output_examples.input: Create hero copy for a reporting tool that helps agencies replace manual weekly reports.
output_examples.output: Headline: Weekly client reports in minutes, not hours. Subheadline: Connect your tools once and send clear performance updates every Monday. CTA: Create My First Report.

output_examples.input: Improve this vague CTA: Learn More.
output_examples.output: Option A: See the Platform in Action. Option B: Build My First Dashboard. Option C: Compare Plans for My Team.

output_examples.input: Write a benefit section for an app that centralizes customer feedback.
output_examples.output: Section headline: Find the patterns behind every request. Body: Bring survey results, support tickets, and sales notes into one view so your team can see what customers ask for most.

best_practices: Provide audience, page type, primary action, and proof points before asking for copy.
Ask for alternate headlines or CTAs when choosing a direction with stakeholders.
Use provided customer language and real proof instead of invented claims.
anti_patterns: Asking for copy without a target audience or conversion goal.
Using broad claims like innovative or all-in-one without proof.
Requesting fake testimonials, unsupported statistics, or exaggerated guarantees.

faq.question: What kinds of pages can this skill help write?
faq.answer: It supports homepages, landing pages, pricing pages, feature pages, product pages, and about pages.

faq.question: Can it improve existing copy?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current copy, audience, goal, and any brand constraints for a focused rewrite.

faq.question: Does it write email campaigns?
faq.answer: No. The skill points users to a separate email skill for email copywriting tasks.

faq.question: Does it create SEO metadata?
faq.answer: Yes. It can provide a page title and meta description when SEO context is relevant.

faq.question: Will it invent proof points or testimonials?
faq.answer: No. It should use proof supplied by the user and avoid fabricated claims.

faq.question: What input gives the best result?
faq.answer: Share the product, audience, page type, main CTA, objections, proof points, and preferred tone.
